iterations.theme: First impressions after the derby win: rain, conditions at Poljud, atmosphere and refereeing

sections.subtitle: An evening for celebration: Hajduk beat Dinamo, and the podcast goes live
sections.screenshot_description: The host opens the show in the studio and congratulates the Hajduk people on the win over Dinamo
sections.content:
The show HŽV Siempre opens in a celebratory tone. The host greets viewers with the words “good evening to good people and those a little less good” and announces that the win must be celebrated worthily. He also emphasizes that he decided to broadcast live, so that the conversation with the audience would stay spontaneous.

The host thanks “more God” that after nervous derbies this time one can “enjoy normally”. He extends congratulations to the whole Hajduk people, the team and all who contributed to the win over Dinamo. He opens the conversation as an evening of relaxed and cheerful analysis of the derby.

The host also joked about the weather: on Saturday at nine in the evening it is, he says, anything but sunny outside. The rainy evening thus becomes the first topic of conversation.

sections.subtitle: Rainy Saturday at Poljud: who sheltered where and who got soaked to the skin
sections.screenshot_description: The host describes how water dripped from the slab on the east stand and how people squeezed together
sections.content:
The host recalls that rain fell for days and did not stop even on match day. He says that, if that is the price of victory, the fans will gladly agree to more rain, so “let's go for a fourth too”. He immediately adds that Europe is far from him and that beating Varaždin on Sunday is much more important to him than thinking about Ajax.

He also describes what it was like in the stands. He himself was on the east side, where, he says, the biggest problem was the slab through which water dripped directly onto people. Because of this the spectators squeezed together, and some withdrew toward the upper parts and onto the steps, where it was somewhat drier. The west side was somewhat cleaner and with more space than the east, so people spread out along the passages.

At the north stand, the host says, “there's nowhere to flee”, so the fans stripped to the waist and enjoyed the rain. At halftime he expected the second half to bring even louder support, since they were already completely wet anyway.

sections.subtitle: The whole team like one Ivan Gudelj: fighting for every ball
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko and the host talk about the players' commitment in the mud
sections.content:
To the host's question whether they are satisfied with the win, Vinko answers in the affirmative. He recalls a comment under one of Hajduk's derby announcements. Someone wrote that it would rain all day, that it would be played in the mud and that Hajduk doesn't have Gudelj. Vinko concludes that “the whole team today was one Ivan Gudelj”, and that is his first thought after the match.

The host agrees and emphasizes the players' commitment, which was clearly seen. He thinks there is nothing to reproach. There were short and stupid passes and an occasional mistake, but they are hard to list. The team fought, and every lost ball it immediately won back and took away.

The host sums up that the win was fought out as a team, and Vinko agrees. He stresses that precisely the fight for every ball and every duel is what has always been asked of Hajduk.

sections.subtitle: Football or water polo: the ball in puddles and a miracle that nobody got injured
sections.screenshot_description: Conversation about the ball that stops in a puddle and the unpredictable pitch
sections.content:
The host says the conditions for playing were unbelievable. As a joke he adds that one chat participant commented that Poljud doesn't need a stadium but a pool. To him, nevertheless, the match was “top” and in the end they laughed. He describes the ball that “goes by water” as a show programme: somewhere it stops where it shouldn't, and somewhere it passes where it isn't expected.

Vinko adds that you never know when the ball will stop, which is the craziest thing. The host says it is a real miracle that nobody was injured. He describes a situation near the end of the match when a player was supposed to dribble the ball, and it stopped in a puddle. It remained questionable how much of that was a mistake and how much a consequence of the pitch. The host emphasizes that from the stand or from the pitch it is hard to think in such madness, because everything depends on will and fight.

More precisely, he says there was everything but blood. He plans to watch the match again in full, because his experience from the stadium is completely different from the television one. It is said that it looks good on television, which he will check.

sections.subtitle: Who controlled the derby: Hajduk was one step quicker, Dinamo without an idea
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko explains why, in his impression, Hajduk controlled the match
sections.content:
Vinko sets aside the “general flood” in which play was up to the knees and gives his impression: it didn't seem to him that Dinamo could do much. He admits he may be subjective, but it seemed to him that the guests controlled nothing. Danger, he says, could come only from some Hajduk slip, as with the first goal. Asked who controls the match, he answers without doubt that it was Hajduk.

The host confirms that Hajduk had more and riper chances. He reminds of Šego, who in the fifth minute missed an incredible chance.

Vinko goes beyond statistics: Hajduk's weakness often used to be being “a step short”, and this time it was a step, or rather half a step, quicker. It was always where it needed to be. He didn't see that Dinamo could do anything independently without Hajduk's help. He admits, however, that in the end Hajduk couldn't either without the opponent's help, and mentions one shot by an opposing centre-back toward his own goal which luckily didn't go in.

sections.subtitle: Birthday greetings, wedding anniversaries and victory beers
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko reads viewers' donations and congratulations in the chat
sections.content:
The show switches to viewers and their donations. The host announces that tomorrow the show's birthday is also celebrated, and Vinko reads a message from one female viewer: Hajduk gave her “the most beautiful gift for tomorrow's birthday”. They congratulate her in advance, and it is also mentioned that during the day one viewer received a wedding anniversary congratulation.

Vinko jokes that everyone got a congratulation that day for something, even without an occasion. It's neither his birthday nor anniversary, but he feels as if he received a gift, and he thanks viewer Marina. A message follows from Ivan Jerković, who sends a donation for a “victory beer” and says that Hajduk lives forever.

The host joins the congratulations. He says he is already dead from tiredness, but hopes he will last until midnight. He also adds that he told his wife it is his anniversary so she doesn't need to buy anything, because the gift is the win over Dinamo. At the end one more message is read, and the host stresses that the small tablet screen is an obstacle to reading.

sections.subtitle: Used to traumas: why Hajduk doesn't know how to celebrate wins
sections.screenshot_description: The host and Vinko talk about caution and avoiding euphoria after the derby
sections.content:
The host states that Hajduk fans don't cope well with wins, because they are used to traumas. Vinko jokingly adds that everyone has “some PTSD”. Then he explains more seriously that in matches like this the fans defend themselves against euphoria and too-frequent praising. On one hand that is good, but beating Dinamo at Poljud in an exciting match that “went out of football frames and into water polo” is still worth celebrating. He doesn't, admittedly, see any of them being the type who immediately praises everything across the board.

The host reminds of reality: it's only the ninth round and 27 more await, so Hajduk hasn't won anything yet. Still, he says, a big thing was done, because Dinamo was beaten at home, and it's a big thing for the coach too, however much he is criticized. For the coach it's the first win in a derby, and he was angry at the press conference too.

The host adds two humorous “good news” items about the coach: that he won the derby and that he lost his voice, which means he led the match.

sections.subtitle: Joke about Imotski: lambs over 40 kilos and returning to the topic
sections.screenshot_description: Relaxed conversation of the host and guests about Imotski and lambs
sections.content:
In the relaxed part of the show the guests and host joke about Imotski. They talk about a man from Imotski and about where lambs are turned (on the spit), with the remark that there “they only spin over 40 kilos”. A guest came up with “small lambs”, and the host adds that lambs of 40 and more kilos are quite usual in that story.

Vinko interrupts the joke and asks them to return to the topic. He suggests they “start talking about the match itself”, because the same happened after the second leg with Raków: after the big win everyone just looked at each other.

sections.subtitle: Exhausting last fifteen minutes: we all came out as if we had played the match
sections.screenshot_description: The host recounts the feeling when the referee extended the match and the post was hit
sections.content:
The host describes that he was at the match and that “it was a flood” in it. He is convinced that everyone, both at the stadium and at home, came out as if they themselves had played the match. Everything “pulled out of him”. The referee added 12 minutes, then let it go up to 15, and the last three minutes, with the post and a shot next to the goal, exhausted him completely.

He explains why: in life the fans have seen too many won matches that in the end spilled away, and he mentions the one from Ukraine. So it was not possible to be relaxed, nor could the win pass easily without drawing out all the energy.

Vinko cites a comparison with the match Hajduk – Anderlecht 2:1, which he attended. He recalls that in the last 15 to 20 minutes Gabrić “worked wonders” and saved the team. The weather was then incomparably better than now, but the audience left quietly, as from a “quiet Mass”. The host adds that Hajduk conceded a goal in the 80th minute from Weber, and Vinko that Gabrić had four saves in fifteen minutes. The host recalls that they were much better in the 60th minute and that Butorović scored a goal, and he himself left cheerful, as he had entered, so the joy lasted until late at night.

sections.subtitle: A crazier derby, but with an excellent atmosphere: the stands sang in water
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 describes the atmosphere in the stands, and Vinko swimming in the 50th row
sections.content:
The first guest considers this one of the craziest derbies he has watched. Although in the city before the match there was no euphoria, in the stands, he says, it was “really good”. People were enjoying, and the atmosphere was excellent in the west, north and east, while the southeast functioned as “one body”.

Vinko adds that he would like all those who decide about new stadiums to come to a match like this at Poljud. Since they are already talking about reconstruction, let them see what it is like when you are in the 50th row and “swimming in water”, and a current of water goes around you. He praises the audience and players, because the conditions were extreme.

The host agrees that the atmosphere was excellent. With that he concludes that the match, despite all the problems with the stands and pitch, showed the Hajduk spirit.

sections.subtitle: Why there is no euphoria: everything is known only after Varaždin
sections.screenshot_description: The host explains that Varaždin is more important than Ajax
sections.content:
The host explains why there is no madness after a big win: everyone knew they were close, but nobody wants to celebrate in advance. The fans, he says, “would most like to bite like a dog”, but they have no knack for it. He thinks euphoria isn't even needed, because one goes from match to match. If they lose or draw with Varaždin, nothing has been done. This year everyone takes these things more rationally, so there is no madness with running on the goal.

Vinko agrees: these three points get real weight only on Sunday, if Varaždin is beaten.

The host admits that Varaždin is ten times more in his head than Ajax. Europe is beautiful, but the championship must be won, because too many years have accumulated. He thinks that when Hajduk takes the championship, all the shackles on hands and feet will be removed and the club will finally be what it is.

sections.subtitle: Un-awarded yellow cards: Kačavenda should have gone off, and Pajač didn't whistle
sections.screenshot_description: The guests analyse the situation with goalkeeper Kotarski and the un-awarded cards
sections.content:
The host reads a message from a viewer who asks about the yellow for obstructing the goalkeeper, and the conversation moves to refereeing. The first guest says it's unclear to him what the referee even whistled in the situation with goalkeeper Kotarski. He says that, after watching the highlights, both that situation and the rest of the refereeing are “the bottom of the bottom”. The host claims that Kačavenda should already in the first half have received two yellow cards, which means he should not have stayed on the pitch. Therefore, he says, there is nothing more to say about the refereeing.

Vinko adds that the goalkeeper's reaction also seems strange to him: it was almost absent. On no recording from two angles did he see a Hajduk player hitting the goalkeeper or a foul even occurring. The host points out that the player entered and cleanly took the ball.

The host compares examples: Brajković was sent off in Osijek for two yellow cards in the first half, while Kačavenda at Poljud, unpunished, made tackles which, he says, are each twice as heavy as Brajković's. Vinko adds examples: Livaja received a second yellow for slamming the ball after a whistle, and today Ivan Sušac a good five seconds after the whistle slams the ball, and nothing is whistled. At that moment, because of weak signal, the broadcast froze.

sections.subtitle: Media, Bruno Marić and the “regime” referee: a sharp reaction to criticism
sections.screenshot_description: The host and the first guest comment on the media space given to Bruno Marić
sections.content:
The host announces that the title of the show is “magnificent victory” because he noticed that sports media are already writing about the mud and grinding down football. He thinks that, had Dinamo won, there would be talk of a magnificent ambience and derby, and now, after Hajduk's win, the media highlight mud and water polo. He doesn't even want to comment on it: let them write, he says, because Hajduk is used to that too, and such stories deserve only mockery.

He sharply lashes out at “those who stole 20 titles” and now talk about referees. He claims that a “regime referee from a regime club” tried to damage Hajduk. He thinks that only after 20 years of such refereeing in Hajduk's favour would it make sense to talk about balance. Vinko adds that these things repeat constantly and nothing changes.

The first guest wonders how it is possible that Pajač did not damage Hajduk, but tried. The host answers: he tried, but did not succeed. The guest then mentions Bruno Marić and asks who gives him space. The host answers very sharply and with criticism, claiming that only those who share his views can give him space, and adds that Marić did not refer to even a single Kačavenda yellow card.

sections.subtitle: Drainage did not hold: a pool at Poljud and a mum cooking in the background
sections.screenshot_description: Conversation about the pitch drainage while the second guest and Vinko comment on leaving the stadium
sections.content:
The conversation returns to the conditions. The host says that the drainage surprised him: he expected the system to hold, but a large amount of water appeared very quickly and nothing drained away. He also said that the drainage “didn't do anything”.

Vinko doesn't agree. He thinks the drainage did work, but the amount of water was simply too great. He recalls the match with Istra, when the rain at one point stopped and the pitch dried very quickly. But such an amount of water falling for so long, he says, is impossible for any drainage.

Meanwhile in the broadcast the background can be heard: the first guest apologizes because his mum is cooking in the kitchen. The others joke that the smell of meat forgives everything. The host mentions that Zoki is getting ready for Tuesday, when there will be “Mrzlo sa Zokijem” and the analysis of the derby.

sections.subtitle: Greetings from Sisak and a weather forecast that was wrong
sections.screenshot_description: The host reads viewers' greetings from Sisak
sections.content:
The host reads viewers' greetings. He sends a big greeting to the crew from Sisak, hopes they successfully made it through to the stadium and reached where they intended. He also greets Davor, Karlo and other viewers following the show.

Then the conversation returns to the weather. The host says that the whole week he was “bombarded” with announcements of a storm at Poljud, and in the morning it rained only in gusts, only later did it flare up. The first guest adds that his iPhone showed 100 percent probability of rain all week, and when it actually rained, the app showed 90 percent. He says the weather forecast was reliable neither in Zagreb nor in Split.

sections.subtitle: Torcida and choreography: a banner that is remembered
sections.screenshot_description: Conversation about Torcida's choreography at the north stand
sections.content:
The host reads a message from viewer Zoran, who recalls one of his favourite banners at Poljud: “Hajduk first, and Pope John Paul second.” The first guest confirms that this match was also good, and Torcida made a “magnificent” choreography.

The host follows up on the choreography at the north stand and describes what impression it left on him. He says that the part tied to a memory of childhood is also interesting, when he and his friends played on dirt pitches and often lost the ball into the school windows. The conversation then turns to dinner and technical preparations.

This part is mostly a relaxed digression before returning to refereeing.

sections.subtitle: Stoppages and added time: did the referee overdo the extra time?
sections.screenshot_description: The first guest explains the reasons for the extension and the stoppages in the match
sections.content:
The first guest returns to the refereeing and recalls a comment he listened to before the show, which comes from the Dinamo side. The commentator explained the reasons for the long extension: an interruption because of the Boys, an interruption because of Torcida, substitutions, so 12 minutes accumulated. The guest thinks the referee could perhaps have reduced the added time.

The host says he has no problem with so much accumulating. The guest agrees, but adds that in the seventh minute of extension the referee let another five minutes run, with rain that additionally made play harder. The host rejects the possibility that the referee wanted to abandon the match: the damage would be great, because Hajduk would have won and that would be the end. He thinks that, if it were abandoned, the match would be postponed for some time, not made up.

sections.subtitle: A referee with no feel for the game: mistakes that are not accidental
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko analyses Pajač's refereeing and the systematic lapses of referees
sections.content:
Vinko assesses that such decisions are made by referees who have no “feeling for football”, and Pajač is, he thinks, one of them. Many of his mistakes come precisely from that: he has no feeling for the game nor for football nor for anyone on the pitch, so he falls from mistake to mistake.

The guests stress that this is not accidental. The host says that after all these years he does not believe in any coincidence. Vinko continues that it is not accidental that such a referee officiates the First League and that he is pushed into matches like this: “it's the whole system”. He admits that the decisions were also to the detriment of other clubs, but the host replies that other clubs don't interest him because for him the decisions were always to the detriment of Hajduk.

The host nevertheless mentions a positive record in derbies with this referee: five wins and three draws. He says that however much the referee tried, he doesn't succeed, and hopes he will come next time too, when Hajduk could raise a sixth win.

sections.subtitle: Kačavenda and the un-whistled yellow cards: “the man shouldn't have been on the pitch”
sections.screenshot_description: The host lists situations in which Kačavenda had to receive a yellow card
sections.content:
The host returns to situations he considered key. He says the intent is visible, and Kačavenda enters the second half and still plays football, although, in his opinion, he shouldn't have been on the pitch. At one throw-in he says it was “throw-in up down”, but he considers the yellow card clean.

He lists several situations. First he mentions a tackle at the opening, and then one more situation when Kačavenda obstructed a player in attack near the top of the penalty area, and “with two feet”. He considers it unbelievable that the player lasted until the end of the match. Vinko tries to clarify which situation is being talked about and asks for context, and then suggests they stop dealing with the referee and turn to nice things about their own team.

The first guest notes that Ante watched the match and so concludes that at least 20 to 22 questionable decisions could be counted. He mentions a corner and one player's elbow, and the host adds that intent accompanies a certain participant every time. The first guest concludes that this match did not inspire confidence in him, and with that the part dedicated to refereeing is concluded.

iterations.theme: Player analysis: goalkeeper, defence, full-backs and midfield

sections.subtitle: A goalkeeper who doesn't inspire confidence: uncertain exits and limp clearances
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 and the Host discuss the goalkeeper's uncertain interventions in the derby
sections.content:
The analysis of individuals begins in goal, and the first impression is flattering to no one. Guest 1 openly says that the goalkeeper “did not inspire confidence” in this match either. The host agrees: nor does he, and he was particularly worried by the situation with the diagonal ball before the conceded goal. He thinks the goalkeeper “could and had to” clear the ball there, not stay in place.

Guest 1 goes a step further and objects to the way the goalkeeper plays with his foot: “He doesn't turn his head, doesn't see what's going on.” According to him, the ball from those kick-outs regularly ends up out. The host adds that at the start of the match the goalkeeper three times in a row missed the ball and that he several times kicked to the wrong side, instead of toward the middle or opposite to what the game required.

**Vinko** singles out two problems that left the strongest impression:

- **limp clearing** of balls from the penalty area,
- **low kicks along the floor**, after which Hajduk in a short period twice served the ball directly to Dinamo players' feet. This happened already in the first half.

Vinko nevertheless admits that the goalkeeper saved what he had to. It seems to him, however, that at the conceded goal he could have reacted better coming out. The host reminds that the goalkeeper in one part of the match saved two shots. One of them was a direct strike by a Dinamo player from which a goal could also have happened. The host is grateful that the opponent decided to shoot directly at goal, and not cross into the five-metre box, because in such a scenario everything could have ended differently. He adds that soon after that the ball could have ended in the net as well had he intervened a little closer.

sections.subtitle: A goal as a sum of lapses: where were the centre-backs, full-backs and midfielders?
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 and Vinko analyse the players' positioning at the conceded goal
sections.content:
The discussion then moves to the conceded goal itself, which turns out not to have been only the goalkeeper's problem. Guest 1 notes that there was almost no space, but that the defenders positioned themselves badly. Del Moral stood behind Hrgović, and the centre-backs he “didn't even see”.

**Vinko** describes what happened on that side. One of our players ended up on the touchline, and the Dinamo player on the wing was free. Vinko says the defender was “somewhere there, but nowhere near where he should be”, although his only task in that phase was to guard the winger. The cross was very quick, so he doesn't blame the goalkeeper either, although he thinks he perhaps had time for a better reaction. He concludes that the goal was “a series of linked mistakes of the whole defensive line”.

Vinko also returns to the kick-outs. He states that goalkeepers often “box” balls that are not for boxing, so the ball flies only three metres and again comes to someone for a shot. The host confirms this: you clear the ball, but you are not in goal, so you create problems for yourself. Vinko reminds that Hajduk conceded a goal to the Spaniards in a similar way, when Stanišić did not clear properly, but into the middle, into the crowd, so the opponents reached the goal with two touches.

The host notes also small lapses at the edge of the touchline. Hrgović twice threw the ball out. Once in the first half he was catching the ball, turned and pushed it out. The pitch was slippery and everyone kept falling. Del Moral in the fifth minute twisted both legs and it looked like he had to go off. The host doesn't know how he played the match to the end because nobody was near him when he tangled himself up.

sections.subtitle: Centre-backs on the scales: criticism of the goalkeeper and praise of Madunić's security
sections.screenshot_description: The host talks about Madunić's security in the back line
sections.content:
Before the ratings of the centre-backs, the participants once more look back at the goalkeeper. Guest 1 gives him a “pass mark” and says he must concentrate. The host adds that the level of security was not the one they have been used to recently. Guest 1 regrets that the goalkeeper no longer seems like before, when he “exuded” security. He hopes he will not irritate more and more, but will return to the old form. The host reminds that until now he was very good and saved “all sorts of things”. All of this is well-meant criticism, and Vinko adds that it is only an impression of the player in that match.

Then the back line comes up. The host opens the topic and states that the best of the centre-backs for him was the player who was close to goal, but in what follows he turns strongly toward **Madunić**. Hajduk had three centre-backs in the match, and Madunić was the best for him “regardless of having been on the pitch the shortest”. The host lists what he saw in the short time:

- four or five duels in the same attack,
- clearing with the foot to the left side from the post and up high to the right,
- two defences with the head, as the tallest in the jump.

He speaks of “a security that we don't have when Marušić and others are on the pitch”. He asks what the coach is waiting for and whether Marušić has to break a leg for Madunić to enter the starting line-up. He adds that Madunić is “a hundred classes ahead”. He alludes to the coach's appearance at the press conference, where he spoke of “gossip and evil tongues”. He asks why a player who is “better than any of our centre-backs” enters only in the 60th minute, and not from the start.

sections.subtitle: A lighter for Kačavenda: “Whistling was enough”
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko and the Host comment on the throwing of a lighter at a Dinamo player at a corner
sections.content:
In the middle of the analysis of the centre-backs the conversation turns to an event from the stands. Vinko mentions that a Dinamo player was hit by a lighter during a corner. Such a sight, he says, is not the same as a welcome for the future Mediterranean Games in Split. He says he sees no sense or need for such an act: “Whistling was enough.”

The host replies ironically and adds that Kačavenda was informed in advance of what awaited him. He stresses that he “could have known everything”, because he knew who he was and how he would be received. He was whistled at during warm-up, at halftime and at every touch of the ball, and the whole stadium was against him.

Guest 1 adds an amusing detail: Torcida “had fun with him for ten minutes at halftime” and warmed him up, and he was whistled at from all sides for all 45 minutes. The host finishes with a joke: if you aren't from Croatia anyway, don't expect to pass without whistling. He suggests that he rather go to Saudi Arabia to earn money than deal with such things.

sections.subtitle: The Mediterranean Games as an opportunity: athletics stadium in Park mladeži and a new football Poljud
sections.screenshot_description: The host explains a possible solution for the stadiums in Split
sections.content:
Thanks to a viewer's donation, the host turns to a topic that occupies Split: it is said that the city could again host the Mediterranean Games. According to his interpretation, this could solve the questions of the stadium and the city.

The host's scenario is as follows:

- **athletics stadium in Park mladeži**, with a capacity of around 20,000 spectators,
- after its completion, moving athletics there,
- **a new football stadium at Poljud** on the site of the existing one.

He sharply criticizes part of the media which, according to him, is trying to portray that the tartan track would have to stay and so there would be no new football stadium. He says the solution is simple. Football is moreover a discipline at the Mediterranean Games, so both athletics and football would be obtained at the same time.

The host follows up on water sports. He says that Split did not build a single pool for the Mediterranean Games and that he has been repeating this for years. He lists clubs and disciplines:

- water polo and women's water polo,
- swimming and synchronized swimming,
- diving,
- diving with fins.

He says it is high time for an indoor pool where children could train in winter. It surprises him that the clubs achieve results in the conditions in which they work. He himself concludes that this is another topic and returns to football.

sections.subtitle: Marušić under the magnifying glass: the worst in defence that Vinko has seen
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko criticizes Marušić's play, the Host offers the opposite view
sections.content:
The return to the centre-backs brings the sharpest exchange of opinions in this part of the show. **Vinko** stresses that the match was “strange” for him for both Marušić and the other centre-back. He doesn't understand what Marušić was trying when before the goal he took over the player on the wing. He is neither agile nor fast enough to close that or get back, and the opponent lofted the ball over. Later he had a tackle that could have been “fatal” for both the Dinamo player and Hajduk. Until the end of the match he only lobbed balls into the penalty area, similar to against Spain.

Vinko concludes that **Madunić** should be in the first 11. By the impression he has gained so far, “he has the calibre to carry Hajduk's defence”, and the others should then agree around him. Guest 1 replies that in the first line-up he has another player, not Marušić, and the Host reminds him that both play in the same position.

The host assesses Marušić more mildly, but with reservations:

- compared to the match against Rijeka, where he was “out of the game” and made more mistakes and a goal was conceded through him, here he was good the whole match,
- he won a few duels at the start, gained confidence and continued to play,
- he doesn't consider his tackle on Kačavenda at all because he thinks that Kačavenda should not have been on the pitch,
- still he showed nothing except what the coach keeps him for: he keeps the ball at the back and tries to push it forward.

Vinko doesn't agree and repeats that a defender must fulfil defensive tasks. Marušić, he says, was in defence the worst of everything he has seen so far. The host counters with Madunić's example: in 20 to 25 minutes he showed everything a centre-back needs, cleans up situations, jumps and wins duels.

sections.subtitle: Hrgović and new maturity: from nervousness to an assist
sections.screenshot_description: The Host and Guest 1 praise Hrgović's play and progress in the head
sections.content:
The conversation about full-backs opens with a joke at the expense of the Zagreb edition of the viewers. The discussion soon becomes serious, because everyone agrees that **Hrgović** was very good. The host praises him for the assist and for good things through the whole match. If there is a mistake, it is small: at one moment he took a corner badly, but “it happens to everyone”, he says.

Vinko singles out his key moves: the cross at the first goal and the **cross to Šego** at the second. The host has a doubt about the first goal, because it seems the ball didn't touch the scorer directly, but “the surroundings hit him”. He admits the cross was nevertheless top-class, and Vinko labels it a gift both to the defence and to the opposing goalkeeper. The host reproaches him for only one thing. He doesn't understand why at one of the corners the ball didn't curl along the ground, but went high into the corner. Vinko supposes that perhaps it didn't sit as he wanted, and such a slow, high cross also appeared.

Guest 1 stresses how Hrgović changed in a short time, as if he “switched from one mode to another”. The host explains it this way: he does not doubt his talent, but the problem for him was always the head. Now he no longer “spreads his arms” and doesn't shake, and the difference is seen both in the match and in training. Guest 1 also adds an important circumstance: the two players on that side understand each other, which makes the whole story easier. The host concludes that Hrgović has matured, the stress level has dropped and he plays without burden and fear.

sections.subtitle: Hot dog instead of ćevapi: a short story from a hungry Poljud
sections.screenshot_description: The host jokes about the food at the stadium
sections.content:
In the middle of the analysis of full-backs the host cheerfully dealt with his food at the match. He tells how, since the rain began and since the match was at three o'clock, he had to set off toward Poljud already around one. At home his wife was cooking lunch, so he had no time to eat.

At the stadium he was disappointed. Everyone expected ćevapi and the audience was told they were going for ćevapi. When they arrived, there were no ćevapi. In the end they had to take a hot dog, that is, a frankfurter. The host jokes asking what kind of hot dog it can be when you expected ćevapi. He concludes the joke with the words: you got a hot dog and you immediately know how you felt.

From the conversation it is seen that in the meantime one of the listeners joined. The host encourages him to freely continue commenting and adds that he is “only a man of” the audience and does not want to interrupt the analysis.

sections.subtitle: Right-back: reliable, combative and always at the level
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 talks about the right-back's reliability
sections.content:
When the conversation returned to the right side, everyone agreed in praise. Guest 1 says he can't remember a single match since he has played in that position in which he was bad or below the level. For him it is a player who “always gives maximum”. In the first ten to fifteen minutes he had small problems with the centre-backs, but otherwise he is correct, combative and “a full hit for a right-back”. Vinko adds that from him you can expect solid or better, “and never less”, and that he plays simply, not complicated. The most important thing, says Guest 1, is not to invent hot water.

The host points to potential. He mentions a statement that this would be a player who could play in the French league and that he is surprised he even came to Hajduk. He thinks that he is currently what the club needs, a safe full-back who has height and helps in jumps, and that was seen at the end of the match as well. Still, he doesn't think he has reached his level: “I expect him to be much, much better still.”

The host also explains the tactics. The player on that side controls the space, while **Hrgović** on the opposite side is more offensive and goes more forward. So the right-back does not have to enter chemistry with the winger, but can be more defensive. Guest 1 would like to see him a bit higher up, but the host reminds that such a role is a tactical decision, not the player's flaw.

sections.subtitle: Del Moral, the midfield guard: doesn't bring forward, but dismantles the opponent
sections.screenshot_description: The host describes Del Moral's destructive role in midfield
sections.content:
The midfield is opened by the host, who stresses that Del Moral enters the starting line-up thanks to the fact that Hajduk won the match precisely through the middle. He reminds that the player twisted his legs in the fifth minute, that in Varaždin he was badly positioned and a goal was conceded then, and now again one goal, but a won match. In his opinion, “we all see that offensively he cannot contribute to Hajduk”. When balls were being cleared, he was among the three-four who in the end ran after the ball. Still, **in the destruction of the opponent's play** he makes a huge difference. “Through that middle they did nothing”, he says, and that is, he says, the key to the win, partly thanks to Del Moral.

The host goes further and considers Del Moral one of Hajduk's best players, right after Bambi, as he calls him. He wants it to continue: it is important that in matches against the biggest rival it is he who brings the edge in the middle.

Vinko agrees that both midfielders were excellent defensively. He especially singles out Del Moral's reading of the game and positioning: how he positions himself, how he understands space and how many balls he took down in the jump. Although he doesn't follow all the statistics, he has a feeling that most of the high balls in Hajduk's half were taken by him. Forward he won't bring much, but he has a “brake” for the opponent, so that doesn't bother Vinko.

sections.subtitle: Don Kera on the horizon: who stands in front of the centre-backs?
sections.screenshot_description: The host praises Don Kera's first touches, Vinko discusses combinations
sections.content:
The discussion about the combination in the last midfield spot passes to Don Kera, whom the host calls a player with an innate feeling for the game. In his opinion, already in the first touches it is seen that he knows which move he will make before he receives the ball. “Those are things you can't learn”, he says. He also thinks that nobody in the league has a better midfield than Hajduk.

Vinko clarifies his standpoint. If Don Kera is in the team and plays as the last midfielder without help from the side, the other can play more forward. If one plays with two sixes, then none of the others can be one of those two. For the last midfielder he wants one of the players to appear “as little as possible, only as an incident and not a rule”. He adds that the other midfielder, if one wants to use him, can be moved forward.

Guest 1 reminds that Del Moral was not brought in as a creative player, but as “the last pillar of defence”, the one who stands in front of the centre-backs. He does that well, and next to him the other midfielder can be freer. By his logic there is no reason for someone else to get precedence over Del Moral. Vinko nevertheless believes that the other player will surely get a chance because “now the madness starts” with the matches.

The host warns that Don Kera is waiting for recovery and will be the first to come in when he is ready. He hopes he will get minutes as soon as possible because he thinks he can bring a lot to Hajduk. Critically he adds that “someone in his head has an idea and his pets”, and then returns to the cold fact: everything depends on health.

sections.subtitle: Six matches in fifteen days: who will carry the dense rotation?
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 and the Host discuss minutes played and squad rotation
sections.content:
Rotations and minutes played become the next topic, and the incentive is the upcoming schedule. Guest 1 reminds that Hajduk expects six matches, including Europe, and the host specifies: fifteen days and five matches. He asks him whether he thinks Mardešić will not play some match.

Guest 1 hopes he won't, but for another reason: every player who is in the roster should be used. He is not for “forcing” only one player, but for everyone being used when needed. He thinks Mardešić should play, but not every match. He also thinks it is wrong to leave material standing aside if it is not used. He reminds that someone asked him whether Garcia would get sacked if he loses a match and adds that this is in the end nevertheless unnecessary. In doing so he remembers saying that one player could play half an hour, and it seems to him he could have.

The host agrees in principle: **a whole match should be played, not only this one, but the last three-four matches**, and whoever is ready should play. He adds, with a fair dose of scepticism, that this would be only “in dreams”.

The discussion briefly brightens with a message from a female listener, which the host uses for a joke and a call for understanding when everyone is tired.

sections.subtitle: “No pets, profiles play”: who slows down the game?
sections.screenshot_description: The host refers to a viewer's comment about the coach's pets and player profiles
sections.content:
The question of the coach's pets is a topic that repeats throughout the whole analysis. The host here quotes a comment of one viewer: in Hajduk there are no pets, but the player profile plays. The host agrees and says that this is “a hundred percent” true and that it should be accepted. Guest 1 answers that he agrees too, but adds: if the profile is the only criterion, the question is whether that profile satisfies what the club wants and needs.

The host and Vinko elaborate what that profile means. Vinko says it is a player who **slows down the game**, which the host confirms: it is a profile without which one cannot play, as is claimed. He wonders whether Hajduk even needs such a slower-down, especially when the team is fast enough. There was talk of an injury that spread, but the host concludes that this profile in no way means that the player is the coach's pet.

Guest 1, with a somewhat ironic tone, notes that it again turns out they are “dissatisfied with the win”. The host replies that he has long been listening to such “fairy tales”, but always says what he thinks. Vinko returns to the midfield and reminds that both midfielders were good. Guest 1 says Del Moral was good defensively, and the other midfielder gave much more forward, which is his task. The host concludes that Hajduk was dominant precisely in the middle of the pitch, where Dinamo was supposed to be strong.

sections.subtitle: A goal conceded as a series of stupidities: from a missed chance to a punishment from the left wing
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 explains why the conceded goal was a series of stupidities
sections.content:
The final part of this unit returns to the conceded goal, about which the participants also spoke at the start. The host briefly describes it as a goal conceded from the left wing after a cross, as opposed to the middle which Hajduk held under control.

Guest 1 insists that **it is a series of stupidities**: “I don't know how it even happened.” He reminds that Hajduk in the fifth minute had a big chance, so it is nice to see how from it, in some fifteen minutes, the opponent's goal came. His thinking is simple: if you don't use a sitter, you must expect to concede a goal. He adds that the goal was “2:1” for the opponent. Vinko supplements that: there was also a bit of luck, and the host adds that Hajduk gave all that itself.

In a relaxed tone the host looks back at a viewer's message about the “friend from the bench”. He tells the viewer that he isn't selling anything and that everyone knows who the “friend from the bench” is. He adds that such bullshit can be justified only by such a friend. Guest 1 says to this that he's not sure who it's about, but supposes. The host then briefly moves to the next topic with the words “Let's move on”.

iterations.theme: Strikers, substitutions and the coach's decisions

sections.subtitle: Wingers in the service of the team: a solid day for one, man of the match for the other
sections.screenshot_description: The host analyses the performance of the winger who scored, with a remark on moves too many and isolations.
sections.content:
After the centre-backs and midfielders, the conversation moves on to the wingers. **Vinko** rates the first of them a three plus. Defensively he was good and committed, but going forward he showed the least of everything he has given so far. Vinko doesn't attribute this to bad form: the game simply developed so that he didn't come to the fore.

**The host** agrees and adds that the player “subordinated himself to the team”. He sees his work also as part of the tactics. By pulling the opposing player inward he opened space for the other winger, so he had enough room to be the best. The host also praises the high press, in which the good triggers were directed upward, and especially highlights the work of Šego and the wing. He reproaches him only for the end of the match: he pushed an opposing player with his hands on the touchline, and already had a yellow card. For a red, he says, it was enough to “pointlessly” push a man who wasn't in play.

**The guest** joins the assessment: the player was purely solid for him, defensively excellent, while in attack there was “much less” than usual. About the other winger, whom the interlocutors call Bambi, the guest says he was combative again. He is sorry that the shot, which bounced and deflected, did not end in the goal, because the player would have deserved it. The guest estimates that Bambi got tired and that he is sorry about the situation in which he slipped.

**The host** gives the most detailed assessment: Bambi is, by him, the man of the match. He lists two-three isolations, breaking through the side “on eyelashes” and a series of good moves in tandem with Hrgović. He reproaches him only for a “move too many” and an open shot that failed, and that is a flaw which, he says, should be solved. The guest remembers a situation in which Bambi slipped under pressure from two players and admits that it reminded him of old days, but adds that the slippery pitch is partly to blame. The host concludes that Bambi is, as always, unpredictable: when you think he has lost the ball, he goes faster forward, and when you think he has passed, he returns back.

sections.subtitle: Psychology at work: the coach, a hug and an appeal to the stands
sections.screenshot_description: The host describes how the coach after the goal ran to the scorer and spoke with him.
sections.content:
The host reminds that the coach at the media press conference asked fans not to laugh at Bambi from the stands when he makes a mistake. Such a player is, says the host, sensitive, needs to be pushed and encouraged, and then he can help the team. **Vinko** accepts this with a remark that it was enough for him to see the player's happiness and heart when he scored and how much that goal meant to him.

The host here notices a real example of a coach's job. According to his description, the coach brought the player into the game, and after the goal ran to him, hugged him and said something to him. The host calls that “psychology” and reminds that he has been talking about it all the time. The coach, he says, must come to the player and lift him, and cheering from the bench is part of that job. In the evening, he jokes, he will probably drink tea because he lost his voice.

**The guest** jokes that the coach is “hungry” for victory and notes that he came to celebrate. The host adds that the coach “knows where his head is” and that last year's derby cost him the championship. He reminds of the red card in the finale of the then-lost match, which additionally increased the weight of this derby.

sections.subtitle: “I will no longer mock him”: a goal that changes the attitude toward the player
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko explains that he will no longer criticize the player after his best performance in Hajduk.
sections.content:
**Vinko** admits that, after all, he has absolutely changed his opinion about Bambi. The player, he says, for three years drove him to sometimes sneer at him, but after today's match and the obvious happiness over the goal he will no longer do so. Vinko credits him with a significantly raised attitude toward the club, the jersey and his own obligations. If he plays badly, the criticism should go toward the coach to take him off earlier, and not toward the player. Vinko rates today's performance as the best he has seen from him since he came to Hajduk and thinks he should be accepted together with his flaws.

**The host** stresses two things. The first is a comparison with last season. In last year's derby the player had a chance for a goal, but didn't use it, while this season he scored. The host sees in this part of the difference between the two seasons and hopes that the goal will be an incentive for the future.

The second thing is the contract. The player's contract expires at the end of the season, and the host doesn't understand what is being waited for. The point, he says, is to have a player who can be cashed in, and not for him to leave halfway through the season or for free. He proposes extending the contract at least for a year until he is sold. He also reminds that everyone once wanted to remove the player, but that it didn't happen. Some things, he concludes, happen for a reason, and some do not.

sections.subtitle: Šego: an assist that saves the day, misses that hurt
sections.screenshot_description: The host and guests discuss Šego, his misses and the assist for the goal.
sections.content:
The conversation turns to Šego and the interlocutors quickly agree that he was a double story. **The guest** recalls that after the match they said that he would have been the worst on the pitch if he hadn't assisted. **The host** admits that he did the high press and ran himself out, but stresses that more than running should be asked of a striker. He lists two situations. In the first he should have converted Bambi's pass which is “incredible to miss”. In the second the ball escaped from his foot while he had his back to the goal, and Livaja, says the host, would have “sucked it in”, turned and scored. The assessment is cruel: in the last three-four-five matches Šego is the worst player, and today too he is among the three worst. The dropping of the ball at the goal deserves praise, while the miss on Bambi's cross was serious. According to the host, in the fifth minute it was harder to miss than to hit.

**The guest** adds that Šego fought through the whole second half, but doesn't know how to receive the ball well and shield himself from the opponent.

**Vinko** agrees that Šego redeemed himself today with the assist and assesses that the player “plays on gusts”. He speaks of a series in which for five matches he is constantly offside or misses what is easier to hit. Last year, he says, he had a phase from the ninth to the eleventh month, and this season he started with a feeling that he could score. He describes Šego as a player who at moments looks bigger than Hajduk, only for big fluctuations in basic things to show up afterwards. The host jokingly says that the “stuff is being saved for Europe” and Ajax, to which Vinko replies that he would sign that.

With Šego the question of the coach also opens. **The guest** stated that it hurts him more that the coach didn't react and that at moments when someone who can score was needed Livaja didn't come on. **The host** asks why Šego stayed on the pitch for the last twenty or so minutes. By him it was precisely he who at the end of the match made the biggest problems: he didn't clear a single ball properly, and before the post the ball went through him. He didn't run out, nor create anything, so the substitution should have been made earlier.

sections.subtitle: Šutalo comes on, and the right side remains an open question
sections.screenshot_description: The host explains why the first substitution was Šutalo and what that says about the coach's vision.
sections.content:
The first substitution was **Šutalo**. Vinko and the host agree that Bambi had entered a phase of tiredness, so fresh legs were needed. **The host** stresses that this move was a good solution for him. Šutalo, he says, was good defensively too, fast and penetrating, and had one shot.

The host wonders why the coach doesn't try Šutalo on the right side. The coach regularly forces him on the left, and Šutalo was brought precisely for the right. He interprets the substitution as “figure for figure” and would want the coach to have gone in with faith in Šutalo as a right-side solution. But he has already seen five times that this is not so, but that a double substitution is made and the player is shifted from one side to the other. Therefore, he says, “Šutalo is OK for me today”, but only as a practical solution.

**The guest** praises him for the shot: he positions himself nicely and quickly looks for a hole in the defence. One shot into the first corner the goalkeeper saved well, although it was not very strong. **Vinko** adds that on a pitch like this a particularly good strike isn't needed to end in the goal and that immediately, as the rain intensified, he was for shooting from distance, because that is hardest for goalkeepers to defend. The guest describes Bambi's goal as a “little frog” that caught the goalkeeper on the wrong foot, and Vinko adds that he nicely covered the ball and that it slightly changed direction, but even without that he would think it would have gone in because it was strong and without a chance for the goalkeeper.

sections.subtitle: Ten million for Šego? The host doesn't believe in fairy tales
sections.screenshot_description: The host ironically comments on stories about selling Šego for ten million euros.
sections.content:
Thereby the host opens the topic of transfers. The story that Šego could be sold for ten million euros sounds unreal to him. Ironically he says that, if that happens, he would “go to an atomic shelter to wait for the end of the world”. It would be good to sell him even for more, but not for five million, and he says that “purely so you have the info”. Ten million for Šego, he adds, could only be given by an association that doesn't follow football and deals with, for example, field hockey.

He would have nothing against some other club taking over the player in the HNL, but he doesn't see who would give such money. He calls all of this fairy tales. If it came to that, it would be good for Hajduk, but it's more realistic to talk about smaller sums.

sections.subtitle: Kadoić, Melnjak and Madunić: what the other substitutions brought
sections.screenshot_description: The host ranks the substitutions and praises Madunić after coming on from the bench.
sections.content:
The interlocutors continue with the other substitutions. The host states that **Kadoić** came on, then **Melnjak** instead of one of the players, and at the end Madunić. The interlocutors are briefly confused about the order, and the host gives his ranking: Melnjak in last place, and Kadoić at the top.

**Vinko** praises one of the substitutions because the player was on every ball, and **the guest** describes the bench player as an “old pit bull”. He slides across the pitch, loses the ball and chases it again, breaks into the five-metre box and crosses. For a player of his age on such a pitch that is, he says, phenomenal, although he did nothing concrete. He came on energetically and with his entry gave a signal that there would be no weakening. The host also positively assesses the role of the tall player who in the finale was to jump for balls crossed into space, because the opponent had a yellow card.

**Madunić** has, according to the host, again shown that he is a player for the first eleven. In a few minutes on the pitch he did everything a centre-back needs: cleans up situations, jumps and wins duels in the jump. The host claims that he is better than all the centre-backs Hajduk has and that he should be given a chance at centre-back, not at right-back. Vinko agrees, and the host adds that Madunić's entry made sense defensively too.

The host adds once more that Šego should have been substituted earlier. He wasn't solving the ball, got stuck in play and was late with the entry of someone who would bring more. Five substitutions, he says, should have been used to keep the team fresh.

sections.subtitle: Win in the derby, lost voice and criticism of the international break
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko conveys Niko Kovač's stance on the three-week international break.
sections.content:
**The guest** says of the coach that he “lost his voice” in several substitutions, but won the derby. In his opinion, it is one of the craziest derbies he has watched, and because of the overall impression, not only because of the play. The trip to the stadium was marked by the international break, so it seemed that Hajduk was being waited for too long. Even worse, he adds, in that period there were no matches that could be enjoyed.

Here **Vinko** remembers what **Niko Kovač** said about the break: three weeks of pause destroy clubs and there is no one to work with. Kovač proposes returning to three windows with two matches each, because the current system disrupts normal work in the club. **The host** absolutely agrees, especially when it comes to clubs that give a lot to national teams. Vinko states that Hajduk gave as many as eleven players to various national teams. The host mentions Dortmund, which practically has nobody to train with.

For the coach the host lists several reasons for praise: the match was turned around after 0:1, with that result they won a derby they hadn't won for a long time, and the coach lost his voice leading the match. He could, he says, be the man of the match along with Bambi. His brain, he adds, is to be praised when needed, and the host wants him to continue that way and win derbies.

**Vinko** hopes that this win could cause a similar effect as the one against Raków, when Hajduk entered Europe. The players would fill with self-confidence and realize that they can.

sections.subtitle: Why is the coach late with substitutions again – or is he not?
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko compares the coach's decisions about substitutions with decisions in a basketball last attack.
sections.content:
**Vinko** admits that during the match the coach's habit of substituting late came to his mind again. This time, however, he sees reasons for a milder assessment. Before the interruption in the 75th minute, when only Šutalo came on, three substitutions were ready. Then came the interruption, the rain intensified, and the coach postponed bringing on three players. Vinko doesn't experience that as a belated reaction, but as a dilemma like in basketball: in the last attack the coach must decide whether to go for a foul and risk free throws or to defend without fouling. It was obvious that the added time would last ten to fifteen minutes, so the entry of fresh players was postponed so that they could reach the end of the match.

**The host** notes that the opponent had by then already made five substitutions, while Hajduk had made none. Vinko agrees that this is usual, because the coach starts to think about substitutions only around the 70th minute. Still, in this match, with a desperate pitch and large expenditure, fresh players were needed precisely in the finale. So this time the decision didn't seem bad to him, but he doesn't know whether it was thought-out or accidental.

The host stays by his view: had the match turned the other way, a different story would now be told. He accepts that the interruptions and the rain are part of the reason, but he would have made the substitutions earlier anyway.

sections.subtitle: A match for Livaja and the question of the midfield line
sections.screenshot_description: The host talks about why this was a match for Livaja and what was missing in midfield.
sections.content:
**The guest** asks whether it isn't presumptuous to say that Hajduk was ready to score another goal if it hadn't been for the interruption. The team conceded a goal in the fifth minute, equalized after two-three minutes, and had a “fury” for a third. **The host** confirms there were chances, but thinks that after the interruption the opponents went on the attack and that then changes already had to be made. He doesn't understand why the coach waits to concede a goal and only then substitutes.

The guest sees the problem in the midfield. The midfield line dropped a little, and the opponent refreshed with substitutions. Someone was needed who can drop to get the ball and keep it as much as he can. **The host** explains that this would be a player who can hold the ball and push it forward, and adds that it's a question how much that was even possible on such a pitch. He understands that the coach didn't go for long kicks and leaves the decision to him this time.

The host's main objection is nevertheless another: for him it was “dead cold” a match for Livaja. He thinks that was seen from the first minute and that the whole story about Livaja and Šego is disputable. Still, he claims that in the end there is room for both the one and the other in the first eleven. With this he concludes the conversation about strikers, substitutions and the coach's decisions in the derby.

iterations.theme: The significance of the win, reactions at Dinamo, the media background and preparations for Ajax and Varaždin

sections.subtitle: Dead tired, a full stand and a week in which one plays every two days
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 tiredly talks about sleepless nights and the good atmosphere at Poljud, the host laughs in the frame
sections.content:
After more than two hours of analysis the conversation briefly descends from tactics to physical reality. **Guest 1** admits that he won't last until midnight and the birthday of one of the viewers whose congratulations were read during the show. His eyes are closing, and since Thursday he has slept only three to four hours. The host throws in that it's similar for everyone.

The guest then sums up the impression of the stands. At the match there were about 24 thousand spectators, “a little fewer than 25 thousand”, and the atmosphere was excellent for him. He again praises Torcida's choreography and stresses that people “deservedly got to enjoy” after everything. Until Thursday, he says, one needs to rest and prepare.

The host reminds of the schedule that follows: **Ajax on Thursday, Varaždin on Sunday**, and Dinamo was only today. He concludes that this is “three matches in eight days” and that the team should be given time to recharge its batteries. He sharply criticizes the Federation for the match times. He thinks it's absurd that again it's played at three in the afternoon, including the Sunday match in Varaždin, and he describes that move in the harshest words.

sections.subtitle: Real, Ronaldo and jokes in the middle of the night
sections.screenshot_description: The host gestures while joking at the expense of Real fans and the story about Modrić
sections.content:
In a semi-serious tone the host reacts to one viewer's comment that many children started supporting Real Madrid because of Modrić. He resolutely doesn't accept the thesis. In his opinion, about 98 percent of the population outside Madrid started supporting Real because of Ronaldo, and not because of Modrić. He adds that for him “the real Ronaldo” is the Brazilian one, and not “some CR7”. Guest 1 joins in with a joke at the expense of his own surroundings who support Real, so the conversation turns into a humorous bickering.

Guest 1 then teases the host with the words that one could get the impression that he is convinced that a slip against Varaždin must be avoided at all costs. He also wonders “what if we lose the next three matches”, to which it is thrown at him that he should simply rest. Vinko jokingly directs him to rest too.

Then follow greetings to viewers and the hope that midnight and the birthday of one of the channel's followers will be reached. The host admits that he himself is “dead”, but that the Hajduk gene doesn't give up.

sections.subtitle: What the win over Dinamo means: a kick up the backside and a six-point difference
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko explains why a win in the derby can serve as a psychological push for the team
sections.content:
The host asks Vinko the key question: how much this win actually means, especially for the atmosphere in the dressing room. He reminds that in the Dinamo environment “cracking” has already begun. Kovačević is mentioned, and a new hitting at Boban is also announced. According to the host's words, there it is madness, while in Split there is peace.

**Vinko** answers that in Hajduk peace is never complete, but that they are used to unrest. For Dinamo, he claims, unrest is an unrealistic situation to which they are not used, so the question is how they will react. From Hajduk's perspective he hopes that this win could mean the same as the second leg of the qualifiers that brought Hajduk the European group: “one more kick up the backside” that will set the team in motion. He says that such matches must be won at home and that the players must realize that they can.

Vinko stresses that these three points get real weight only if Varaždin, which “comes in eight days”, is beaten on Sunday. The host adds that those are actually six points. Vinko calculates: three points more for Hajduk and three fewer for Dinamo, so the difference shifts by six. The same calculation, he says, held last season too, when Hajduk won twice at Poljud so the difference of 18 points was reduced to 6, which significantly changed relations and the impression of the entire season.

He also assesses the circumstances of the win. Hajduk won in a turnaround and after a very stressful match. He reminds of the defeat in Rijeka 3:0, in which all three goals came from individual mistakes, although the idea of the game and its execution, in his opinion, were not that bad. After such a defeat and a three-week break, returning to a derby at home was hard. The end of the world would not have come even if Hajduk had lost, but it would have been hard to get out of such a defeat. Vinko believes the players felt pressure, even a kind of imperative of victory, and that they played a manly match.

sections.subtitle: Ajax as “team building” and the final against the Dream Team
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko smiles while comparing the match with Ajax to “team building” without expectations
sections.content:
Vinko stresses that earlier it was said that derbies must be won “somehow”, even by force. This time, he says, the win wasn't only by force because there was also quite a lot of play. He hopes that the team will not get carried away because of Ajax. He experiences the match with the Dutch club as “team building” from which nothing is expected, except that the players “don't take off their underpants”.

The host follows up that Varaždin on Sunday is a far more important match. Vinko illustrates it with a comparison: Varaždin is “like a final against the Dream Team in Barcelona”. Ajax is thus a reward and an opportunity for relaxed play, and the real stake is the league.

In the same part of the conversation Vinko mentions that he decided not to answer one viewer because such questions “no longer make sense”. He suggests that the conversation return to what matters, and that is the team.

sections.subtitle: If Dinamo had won: the coach would be under fire
sections.screenshot_description: The host explains what would have happened had the derby ended in Dinamo's favour
sections.content:
The host adds a scenario that in his opinion Vinko did not fully elaborate: what would have happened had Dinamo won. He is sure that “the coach would be hit from his own weapon”. Hajduk's coach, claims the host, has not yet won any derby, and the other important matches were not even close to a positive outcome. Had the win not come, a “circus” would have arisen, there would have been laughing and mocking, and the opposing camps expected that.

The expectations were, according to the host, quite the opposite of the outcome. Everyone counted that Hajduk would slip again and that it could be mocked, but now the atmosphere is reversed. Those “from the opposing camps” pulled the handbrake, and now, he says, are hiding in “mouse holes”.

The host also looks at Dinamo's coach. He thinks that he himself decided to become the Dinamo coach so he had to know what that brings. He describes the job of the Dinamo and Hajduk coach as the most stressful in Croatia, with stress 24 hours a day. As examples he gives Hajduk's coach Garcia and Gattuso, of whom he claims that a year in Hajduk was “like five years”. In that comparison he states that the most important thing is to stay healthy and that such a function needs to be accepted with all its consequences.

sections.subtitle: Momentum is on Hajduk's side, and disorder in the Dinamo dressing room
sections.screenshot_description: The host reads comments from portals and concludes that the momentum has passed to Hajduk's side
sections.content:
The host concludes that the momentum has gone to Hajduk's side. The win, he says, brought Hajduk “a lot of good things in the dressing room”, while at Dinamo the situation is the opposite. In doing so he reads a viewer's comment that he is too harsh toward the rival and replies that he is more than objective. He advises him to open Index and other portals and see for himself how much negative is written about Dinamo.

According to his description, disorder reigns at Dinamo: people are insulted, and the drive to Zagreb after a defeat is not pleasant. In contrast, Hajduk's momentum is usually good at this part of the season, but one must also learn to cope with wins. “It's not easy to cope with wins”, says the host, and the continuity of winning is the key to everything.

He says that Hajduk with this win has done nothing if it doesn't win in Varaždin as well. That Ajax the players should play relaxed (“play whatever happens”), and Varaždin on Sunday is very important. Vinko adds that one only shouldn't turn out ridiculous against Ajax. Losing is fine, but “lose like men”. The host notes that a relaxed player is often better too.

sections.subtitle: Bruno Marić and the question of who gives him media space
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko reads a comment about Bruno Marić, the host grumbles in the background
sections.content:
Vinko reads how Bruno Marić comments that Dinamo was wronged and that referee Pajač wronged Dinamo because of one sending-off. He draws an ironic comparison: Marić talks about honesty like Tomo Horvatinčić about traffic. The host continues that comparison with a crude joke about driving.

The host then expresses disgust that such a person is given media space at all. He hopes that Šapić got fired at HRT precisely because he again ceded public space to Marić. He also reminds that Šapić went to the water polo federation as a spokesman. He describes Marić as a man who is, in the questions of Croatian football, including referee instructors, immoral, and calls his involvement in the selection of referees a disgrace. He states also that after earlier matches he praised referees for “excellent refereeing”. All of this are his assessments.

The host wants Sportske novosti and similar media to experience a “boomerang”, that is, to turn against those who give a voice to such people.

sections.subtitle: Ninth round, 27 rounds ahead of us and “Mediterranean unrest”
sections.screenshot_description: The host stresses that it is only the ninth round and nothing has been won
sections.content:
Reading a viewer's message reminding that it is “only the ninth round”, the host agrees. 27 rounds remain, and Hajduk could still find itself 18 points behind Dinamo. Because of this he doesn't want to exaggerate with euphoria, nor celebrate one win as if the title had been won. He adds that often, when Hajduk wins a derby, it is asked why the fans are not satisfied, and in fact it is just a sober approach.

The win Hajduk deserved and tonight can rejoice. Tomorrow is a new day, five days to Thursday, “the little birds sing and nobody honks on the road”. But nothing more than that has been done: no title has been won nor a key match won, although it is possible that this match was key, and that will be seen only through the season.

The win brings an edge to one dressing room, peace in one and unrest in the other. At Dinamo a circus and nervousness are expected, while in Split the “Mediterranean madness” has calmed down and the way of communicating Hajduk is used to. Vinko adds that unrest is the natural environment of the Hajduk team, but not of Dinamo's.

sections.subtitle: A statement from a sports show that Vinko had to read four times
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko reads from the screen a statement from a sports show, the host listens in disbelief
sections.content:
Vinko, who normally doesn't follow the show “Sportsko jutro” with Olivari and Lončarević, says that after the match clips immediately appeared for him on the internet. He reads a statement: how in “about an hour that one could play” Dinamo “showed to be the better team, more secure”, but that it showed that with nothing concrete. He admits he read the sentence four times to check whether his eyes had deceived him, and then in the article he saw that it was indeed written that way.

The host supposes that the statement could be Olivari's and without hesitation calls it stupidity about which there's no sense even discussing. Vinko clarifies that it's an interview after the match in Sportske novosti, and he came across it searching for content about the sports morning. In doing so he predicts that Monday in that show will be “merry”. The host announces that he will watch it.

In conclusion, it was announced that Zoki will meticulously dissect the whole media picture about the derby on Tuesday.

sections.subtitle: Hrgović in the national team: does he deserve a call-up or must he still grow?
sections.screenshot_description: The host states his opinion on Hrgović's call-up to the national team, Vinko shakes his head
sections.content:
Viewer Lord asks whether Hrgović should be in the national team. **The host** thinks he should and that the national team coach must call him, because “there is still time and space”. He admits that there are better wingers, but says he is definitely among the candidates who should get a chance. With that he follows up with a doubt: for Hajduk at this moment it may even be better that the national team doesn't call him until the club solves the buyout, so that complications don't arise. Still, he claims that the next gathering without him is “below any level”, because the national team is deficient in that position.

The host reminds that some players were pushed into the national team after only one good match, while for Hrgović not even a call-up is considered. **Vinko** has the opposite stance: until he starts to decide big matches, he shouldn't be called. He thinks he has not yet outgrown his generation. He is excellent and important in the young national team, but the senior level is not yet right for him.

The host partly agrees and asks that he first decide the matches against Belupo, Istra and Lokomotiva. He stresses that he has nothing against the player, but at that level his performance does not yet justify a call-up. Still, he assesses that this is a player for whom there is both time and space.

sections.subtitle: Ajax or Varaždin: which is more important?
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko and the host agree that the match with Varaždin is more important than Ajax
sections.content:
Vinko reads a comment by a viewer who said before the match that with a win in the derby Hajduk doesn't lose against Ajax, and surely puts Varaždin in order, and that the biggest self-confidence goes to Garcia with his team. Vinko agrees with that, but repeats that the match with Ajax isn't that important to him. Far more important to him is the win against Varaždin on Sunday.

The host resolutely adds that he doesn't think Ajax needs to be beaten. “I think we have more important matches in Europe”, he says, and those are the ones against the Swiss opponent and the Gibraltar team. Ajax is for him a reward for the first nine rounds in the league, and much more important and key is the win over Varaždin. He wants “a real manly win by a couple of goals”, because Varaždin people once won against Hajduk by such a margin, so now they should be repaid in the same measure.

For Europe he estimates that six points should be taken in the matches against weaker opponents and if possible one more point, to get through the group. But even that is not obligatory: if it doesn't succeed, “it's not the end of the world”. All efforts should be invested in Hajduk being champion.

sections.subtitle: Europe without imperative: a draw that favours Hajduk
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko explains why the first European appearance against Ajax is a good draw with no expectations
sections.content:
The host stresses that if the title in the league is won, next season Europe comes again by itself, and the first season in Europe after a long time, with a long break of 16 years, must be a big test for the team and the club. Hajduk should grow slowly from year to year and learn what it forgot long ago.

Vinko adds that steps must not be skipped: this year the European school is going through, and next year, God willing, it won't be the same story because not all 23 players and the whole staff will change. Now Hajduk enters Europe “incognito” and doesn't know how it will react, but the starting position is good: the first match at home against one of the biggest names. Because of that nothing is expected, and every result that is not a defeat would be a “tremendous tailwind”.
