The host reminds of history: Hajduk against Ajax, which was the winner of the UEFA Cup and champion of the Champions League, drew 0:0 at home and beat it 1:0 in Ljubljana, where it played as the home side. So nothing is impossible, but the match with Varaždin must not be subordinated to Ajax.

Vinko imagines an alternative: had Hajduk played the first match away in Gibraltar on artificial grass, any drop would be understood as a tragedy. The host warns that Gibraltar must not be underestimated: the Gibraltar team against Rijeka played well, and Zvezda also won there only 1:0 from a penalty. Nobody had a good time there.

sections.subtitle: Mrzlo sa Zokijem and an appeal to viewers: questions, likes and subscriptions
sections.screenshot_description: The host invites viewers to ask questions and subscribe to the channel
sections.content:
The host announces “Mrzlo sa Zokijem” on Tuesday and invites viewers to fill their fridges with beer because all the “expert and non-expert analyses” from the next two to three days will be dissected on the show. Zoki will, he says, “salt” all that, and at the same time Ajax will be previewed. Viewer Mario Gudić jokingly mentions that Čeferin is “pushing Hajduk”. The host also greets the show “Duga lopta” which on Wednesday will speak about similar topics.

The host then asks viewers to post questions so that the show would last another 25 minutes, and he and Vinko would hold out until midnight. He appeals also for subscription: only few viewers respond to “subscribe”, so he asks for likes and sharing because of the algorithm.

Vinko answers viewer Arkan who asked whether he is on TV tomorrow. He isn't, because after the match with Ante he only did a short live. The host himself listened to nobody because he was at the match. There is also talk about broadcasts: the host watched the summary on Hajduk Digital TV, and heard that the announcer of Max TV was calling for the match to be abandoned. Vinko says he did not experience the commentator of Hajduk Digital TV, whose surname is Puškar, as particularly biased. Even he was surprised at what Pajač was doing.

sections.subtitle: Cheering against Ajax, jokes about players and “we can do it”
sections.screenshot_description: The host answers a viewer's question about cheering against Ajax and the expected full Poljud
sections.content:
Viewer Mata asks whether even better cheering is expected against Ajax or whether rain is needed again for “madness in the stands”. The host rejects the connection with rain. The match had good cheering and a good choreography, but with nothing spectacular compared to what he himself experienced at Poljud. For Ajax he expects a full stadium and stronger cheering.

A viewer's joke follows about the player who came on in the 90th minute plus 14. Vinko asks what that player should think after such an entry and adds that he increasingly reminds him of Hugo, with the saying “the mountains shook, a mouse was born”.

Viewer Vibor Cicvarić asks about Ajax's possible line-up and mentions Nejašmić. The host answers that Hajduk “can do it”: it played against Ajax that had won the UEFA Cup and the Champions League and drew 0:0 at home, and in Ljubljana won 1:0. Again he stresses that Varaždin is much more important, but if Ajax is beaten, “God grant”.

Toward the end of this part Vinko jokes that they have “cheered up” the viewers so they are going to lie down, and the host replies that they promised to stay until midnight, because that is the Hajduk gene and they do not give up. The reading of questions continues, among which is the one about lighting flares toward the stand for the disabled.

iterations.theme: Viewers' questions: incidents, goalkeeper, title race, transfer window and conclusion

sections.subtitle: Flares at the stand for the disabled: “That is the bottom of the bottom”
sections.screenshot_description: The host indignantly comments on the throwing of flares at the stand for the disabled, Vinko listens in the frame.
sections.content:
During the evening viewers continued to bombard with questions, and the first one referred to one of the ugliest scenes from the match. Viewer Živanović asked what the host and Vinko think about the flares that the supporters of the visiting team threw toward the stand for the disabled.

**The host** doesn't hide his outrage. He calls throwing flares at the disabled a disgrace and a “fistful of misery”, a level below which one can hardly fall. He says he doesn't know what he would even say about people who are not ashamed to target a stand with persons with disabilities. He adds that anyone sitting on that stand, who sees that someone throws a flare at them, would remember it for the rest of their life.

**Vinko** stresses that he doesn't defend any incidents or excesses, but warns about double standards in media reporting. He reminds how much was written about how Torcida “destroyed the stadium” in Gorica, so he wonders whether a single sentence will be devoted to this case. He thinks that the burning of stands and breaking of chairs are constantly talked about, while such things are never mentioned.

The host follows up with the same suspicions. He says he'll see the “heroes” of Sportske novosti, Večernji list and Index, who used to moralize over chairs and make a circus around them. He is interested whether they will debate also the morality of throwing flares at the disabled, which according to his words is also a criminal offence. He himself answers that probably there will be nothing.

sections.subtitle: Fear for the winger: why Bomba's injury was no joy to anyone
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko explains why he was worried about the injury of the winger Bomba.
sections.content:
The conversation then moved to the winger whom they call Bomba in the show. Vinko asked how many fans were happy that Bomba allegedly got injured with the national team and therefore wasn't in the starting line-up.

**Vinko** admits that he himself wasn't happy. Bomba, he says, started to play much more serious football than had been seen from him so far, and Vinko was also afraid because of the history of his injuries. He reminds that in two-three instances the same thing happened. Just when the player would show progress and become useful to the team, a knee, ankle or shoulder would show up, and he would be missing for a month or two, and after that he would be completely unusable. Therefore, he says, he feared it was not an injury that would set him back four steps.

**The host** also wasn't among those who would rejoice at the injury. He thinks Bomba can be useful at any moment, at least thirty minutes. He can “make a circus on the pitch”, stir up the game, break through the side and cross or score, even from the bench. He honestly admits that, knowing the coach, he nevertheless prefers that he was absent unrecovered rather than immediately end up in the starting line-up. According to him, the coach wouldn't put him on the bench as an option, but among the first eleven.

The host sums up Bomba's advantages and flaws simply: flaws should be hidden, and virtues highlighted. The slippery pitch at the derby suited him, and had it been dry, he might have made an even bigger show. He is most useful, he thinks, as a player who is given space and who can turn a match around.

sections.subtitle: Debate about goalkeeper Silić: tolerate or replace?
sections.screenshot_description: The host defends goalkeeper Silić and recalls his junior days in the academy.
sections.content:
Viewer Čačić asked whether Silić should be removed from Hajduk's goal. He thinks it would cost them both in Europe and in the league.

**The host** clearly opposes. He would keep tolerating Silić because, as he says, they aren't slips that cause the team big problems. He reminds that Silić was already in the academy a goalkeeper who was talked about, the presumed next number one, and that he defended the goal in the final of the junior Champions League. Then he got injured so Borna Buljan jumped in and did a top-class defence in Dugopolje. The host admits that Silić has slips and that he can do something stupid and concede a goal, but equally he defends things that wouldn't be expected from him. He concludes that he is developing in a good direction. Some need more time, some less.

The main argument is the lack of an alternative. Ivušić is, according to the host, every now and then ill or injured, and Dante Stipica left football, although he was begged to stay. When a year and a half has already been given to the player, he should be given a chance to the end and the maximum drawn out of that project. He thinks that by removing him nothing would be gained, and a lot would be lost.

**Vinko** adds that if Hajduk were fighting for the title, one would need to have a goalkeeper who at that moment is better than Silić in order to remove him. He recalls a similar situation with Lučić, who started to make incomprehensible mistakes, because of which a good part of the championship slipped through the fingers. Then another goalkeeper came to the goal who proved capable of carrying such a moment. Today, says Vinko, among those available he doesn't see such a goalkeeper, except Dante who is at the sunset of his career.

Both agree that the key is in the approach. The host claims that a player must be under pressure and aware that at any moment he can end up on the bench. Vinko stresses that Silić is a young lad who must learn, work and progress. While he behaves like that, he is there to be the first goalkeeper.

sections.subtitle: Title race: Dinamo the favourite, Hajduk competitive, Rijeka lurking
sections.screenshot_description: The host analyses who is the favourite for the champion's title.
sections.content:
Ivan Cvitanović asked who has the greater chances of winning the HNL, Hajduk or Rijeka. The host answered more extensively.

**The host** thinks Dinamo is still the biggest favourite. Not because of players or coach, but because of everything that stands behind it. He claims that referees have been known to bring Dinamo points, mentions games around red cards and matches, and concludes that Dinamo is the favourite because it is “pushed” to be champions, and not because they are legitimate favourites. Hajduk, in his opinion, has an absolutely competitive squad. He sees a fight of Hajduk and Dinamo, and Rijeka might depend on events in the club itself. In doing so he warns that Dinamo and Hajduk play Europe, so a fatigue of material can occur which Rijeka can exploit. He considers a race of three good for Hajduk, and if Varaždin and Osijek take points off everyone, that is, he says, the way in which Hajduk can become champion.

**Vinko** notes that with the current state of the table the difference in points is small. It wouldn't surprise him if someone else got involved in the race, for example Osijek or Varaždin, but he thinks it is too early for that. Hypothetically he adds that at Dinamo a coach change can happen and reminds of the season when they changed four coaches. That would not necessarily improve their play, and could take everything in the club even worse.

The host reminds that only a quarter of the season has been played. It remains to be seen how the team will react to Europe and how many points its expenditure will cost it. For that there is no pattern on which one could base. Vinko concludes that every prediction for champion at this moment has a big coefficient.

sections.subtitle: Meeting of Luka and Marko: friends from the national team beyond fan divisions
sections.screenshot_description: The host comments on the meeting of Luka Modrić and Marko Livaja after the match.
sections.content:
Viewer Ivica Blažević asked for a comment on the meeting of Luka and Marko after the match. It concerns Luka Modrić and Marko Livaja, who met at Poljud.

**The host** explains that he saw when the asker entered the stand, but it was late to say hello. About the meeting he supposes that Marko came because of the children, who took photos with Modrić. Everyone chatted nicely. He especially stresses that Modrić at Poljud, in the club he has supported since childhood, was delighted and nicely hugged Livaja. He mentions also announcements that Modrić could return to the domestic league, with a contract for a year until the European championship. He concludes that first loves are never forgotten.

**Vinko** doesn't see this as anything unusual. They are former teammates and winners of a bronze medal, so it is normal that they greet each other. The only question is when they last saw each other.

The host here concludes more broadly. The fans are divided into Hajduk and Dinamo supporters, but the players who go through the younger national categories know each other, often share rooms and are in private contact. The essence of sport is socializing, friendship and competition, while the fan side is another dimension. From his own experience in water polo he adds that whenever he comes to some city, he calls an acquaintance athlete and is always welcomed.

sections.subtitle: Miki Rapaić and other “characters”: dressing-room anecdotes that nobody writes any more
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko retells an anecdote about Miki Rapaić from Istanbul.
sections.content:
In a conversation about friendships among players, Vinko recalled anecdotes that he read in a short video. He didn't know the speaker's name, only that he is a Serbian former footballer.

**Vinko** retells that this footballer played with Miki Rapaić in Istanbul and that those were the happiest days of his life. Even today he praises him as a man and as a footballer, with countless anecdotes. One is about how Miki in the morning at training begged a teammate to slide-tackle him so that he could go sleep. When he slid in, Miki screamed and held his leg, they took him away, and he went home. He showed up only the day after next, as if nothing had happened.

Vinko also cites another story, about a teammate whose name he doesn't remember. On an auxiliary pitch with a small stand, behind which is a wall and a meadow, someone kicked the ball over. That player went to fetch it and did not return. They continued to play without him and after some fifteen minutes waited for a new ball, and nobody saw him the whole day. The next day at training he appeared with the ball, barely arriving after 24 hours. Vinko concludes that those were special characters, he and Miki, and that unfortunately there are fewer and fewer of them.

**The host** adds that today everything would be filmed and end up in headlines. We live in a virtual world in which everything is filmed and published, so young people have become cautious.

At the end of this part the host congratulates the birthday of a viewer nicknamed Nastupa, to whom he wishes health, happiness and that Hajduk brings the title this year.

sections.subtitle: Max TV, speakers and referees: “It began from the first match”
sections.screenshot_description: The host answers viewers about the broadcast on Max TV and the refereeing of Hajduk.
sections.content:
Two viewer questions touched on the broadcast of the match and the refereeing.

The first asked whether it is possible that on Max TV the Dinamo fans are heard more, while on Hajduk Digital TV everything is heard normally, from the commentators to the fans, especially Torcida. **The host** replies that it is possible and reminds that Zoki says that on Max TV speakers are placed beneath the Boys. That is, he says, a classic story and part of a wider picture in which everything is harnessed, from Sportske novosti to Večernjak.

Jerko asked when Marić and his referees will start again against Hajduk. **The host** thinks they have already started, he doesn't know when they stopped. By him, it started from the first match Hajduk played in the HNL and will last until the last round. He doesn't see even a possibility that this changes. He explains that referees are raised through a system in which from the youngest matches Hajduk is refereed as Hajduk, and Dinamo as Dinamo. Whoever doesn't referee that way cannot become a referee, so nothing can be expected from those who enter from such a base either.

**Vinko** sums this up in one sentence: it is a continuous process.

The host then concludes that he will not dwell further on ugly things because Hajduk won.

sections.subtitle: Euphoria and Ajax: “Let it be team building”
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko explains why the match with Ajax should be experienced as team building.
sections.content:
Viewer Saša asked whether a possible win against Ajax could be dangerous, because it would create too much euphoria around the club and the players could get “conceited”.

**Vinko** reminds that they already said that in principle. The match with Ajax should be understood as team building, and not as something around which to create euphoria, depression or fame. Although he doesn't want to call it a friendly, he thinks Hajduk has nothing to lose there, and every result that is not a defeat is a “super gain”.

**The host** admits that euphoria always hangs over their heads like a sword and that Hajduk is prone to it. Regardless of that, he says that one simply has to go on.

Vinko adds that euphoria at this moment can seize part of the fans, but that by everything seen the team should not go into those waters. He looks at it that way, he stresses, on the basis of the impression he has gained.

sections.subtitle: Hunger for a place in the first team: bench, academy and players on loan
sections.screenshot_description: The host lists Hajduk's players on loan and the clubs in which they play.
sections.content:
The best guarantee that the team won't relax, thinks **the host**, is the large number of players who think they deserve a place in the first team. He asks how many of them stayed on the bench at the derby, and answers that quite a few. As long as there is hunger and desire to prove oneself, Hajduk will, he says, be competent in all competitions.

Besides the bench, he is convinced that in the academy there is a heap of players who want to jump into those places and week after week show that their place is there. As an example he lists Hajduk's players on loan and in reserve teams:

- **Uskok** beat Dragovoljac 4:0 and leads in the Third League.
- **Croatia** is near the top of the second league.
- **Hajduk 2** is high in the fourth league.

The host concludes that this is the way to go, proving oneself week after week.

sections.subtitle: Šego and Livaja: two different profiles, one big question
sections.screenshot_description: The host responds to criticism over his rating of Šego and talks about the difference in profile with Livaja.
sections.content:
Viewer Mario Gudić wrote that the host spreads intolerance toward Šego, that Šego is not to blame that Livaja “has gone to ruin” and that Šego could next summer leave for four-five million.

**The host** replies that he says what he sees. Šego is for him the worst player of the last five matches and, he says, if the viewer doesn't see that, that is his problem. He reminds that someone earlier spoke of a sale for ten million, and he himself considers four-five million more realistic. He stresses that he has nothing against Šego and that he has said several times that both Šego and Livaja can play.

The claim that Livaja “has gone to ruin” he rejects as fiction and fantasy of those who would wish it. He adds that Livaja doesn't need to be compared with Šego at all because they are two completely different profiles. Šego has advantages that Livaja doesn't have, and Livaja has things that Šego will never have. Hajduk, he claims, needs both the one and the other, but the other is not used. Why that is so, he leaves as a big question.

sections.subtitle: Transfer window: centre-forward, centre-back and the question of whom to bring
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko talks about the need for another striker and about Martin.
sections.content:
The last question of the evening related to the next transfer window: what kind of player profile should be sought to strengthen the starting line-ups.

**The host** is not sure that Hajduk needs any specific profile at all. He would possibly consider a centre-forward, but immediately wonders whom to bring, because such a player would sit on the bench. He mentions that Livaja is already used in that role, and the question is whether the player sits on the bench or Šego plays. The key, then, is which profile would accept sitting on the bench.

**Vinko** would gladly have another centre-forward because the striker Martin has so far not shown that he should be kept until the end of the season. If that lad doesn't pull himself together, Vinko would return him at mid-season to Atletico. He reminds of a similar situation with Hugo last season: the club saw what that player can do, but had too little use from it because he didn't play with heart either. For Martin he still doesn't want to pass a final judgement, but at this moment he sees the need for one more striker.

The host would, when it comes to defence, consider a left centre-back. He thinks that the club has solutions from its own programme, and Gabrić and Madunić he mentions as a possible centre-back pair. As for the last midfielder, it depends on Don Kera, whom they haven't yet seen. If he shows himself, a number six need not be sought, and if not, then it is definitely a priority.

sections.subtitle: Conclusion: a win to enjoy, an opinion that is not an insult
sections.screenshot_description: The host and Vinko say goodbye to viewers at the end of the show.
sections.content:
The show reached its end after more than three hours live, and the host admits that everyone is tired. He invites viewers to leave likes and comments, with a note that they will again discuss topics that they didn't get around to.

**The host** reminds that he appears with a personal opinion and doesn't want to impose a stance on anyone. If viewers are satisfied with what he said about Šego or not, they can freely write, and he will respond. He thinks that this is not insulting, but stating what he thinks, and that is the meaning of the whole show. He adds that he is not there to “wrap up” his opinion “in a package”.

He announces also a new slot on Tuesday, when the show expects a continuation of the analysis and viewers' questions that they didn't manage to answer today.

**Vinko** thanks and says everyone is tired, but “healthily and cheerfully tired” after an evening like this. The host hopes that everyone surely got home, especially Joško who is travelling from Split. He stresses that Hajduk won and that this win should be enjoyed: tomorrow morning with coffee, little birds and the television, and without fear of reading Sportske novosti too, with a laugh. The show ends with a greeting until we see each other soon.
